world.eraEvidence: two modern hosts discussing a self-help book; phone, banking app, email, traffic and kitchen life are present-day
world.setting: A modern podcast-style conversation about everyday emotion, money, work and relationships, staged in ordinary present-day rooms and streets.

ellen.look: a woman in her early 30s, medium build, shoulder-length brown hair, wearing a simple cardigan over a t-shirt, modern casual clothes

marcus.role: calm host who explains the book's ideas with everyday examples
marcus.look: a man in his mid 40s, slim build, short graying hair and a light button-up shirt with rolled sleeves, modern casual clothes

reader.name: The Reader
reader.role: everyman listener who is stuck in worry about money, work or relationships
reader.look: a tired adult in their late 30s, average build, messy dark hair, wearing a grey hoodie, sitting at a kitchen table at night

kitchen.look: a small modern kitchen at night, a leaking ceiling stain above the sink, a laptop open on the table

cafe.look: a busy noisy cafe with clattering cups and crowded tables, warm lights

highway.look: a foggy highway at night with gridlocked cars and a steering wheel in view

office.look: an open-plan modern office with desks, monitors and a clock on the wall

objects.why: the book's central metaphor: feelings as an internal compass pointing toward relief or away from it
the everyday screen of worry, banking apps and notifications
the steering wheel and traffic: a feeling of being stuck or moving forward
the path toward the desire; choices as turns in the road
the place where the reader lives with the leak and the bills
focus on the desire, aiming the attention
feeling good versus bad, the emotional signal
the desire already received in thought, appreciation as a gift

spine.claim: Positive-thinking routines fail because the feeling underneath is still heavy; the reader is not broken, the compass is just being ignored.
Feelings are guidance, not verdicts: the emotional scale shows which direction your focus is pointing right now.
Contrast is not punishment; the bad feeling is the signal to turn attention toward what you want.
Allowing and appreciation change the feeling in daily life, without forcing or denial.
Your current feeling is not a verdict on your life; it is the next reading of your own compass.
